steps.path: Marketplace → the row under the featured banner
steps.headline: The type switch names every kind of thing you can install: Plugins, Skills, Specialists, Tools, Prompts, Themes.
steps.changed: Two choices (Plugins | Themes) became seven, each with a count. 'Tools' is the word for MCP servers; 'Specialists' is the app's word for agent definitions.
steps.notice: Skills 22 counts skills that live inside plugins too — pick Skills and every one of them shows up on its own. All 42 counts only what the grouped view shows.
steps.risk: Seven words is the widest this row has been; below about 1000px the vibe chips wrap to a second line. The phone version is step 9.

steps.path: Marketplace → any rail or the grid
steps.headline: Every card says who made it and whether it was checked — two small marks, never a score.
steps.changed: Under the author: YouCoded / Verified / Community (who published it) and Checked / Caution / Not checked yet (the automatic check on this version). Hover either for the plain-words meaning.
steps.notice: Green dot = checked, amber = caution with a count, grey = not checked yet. Grey is deliberate: most mirrored items start unchecked and red everywhere would be noise.
steps.risk: The badge row costs one line on every card; rails get a little taller.

steps.headline: Thumbs-up percent replaces the star rating, and risky abilities show as small glyphs at the right.
steps.changed: Bottom row is now: 👍 93% · installs · what's inside · then glyphs for runs-commands, uses-internet, needs-a-key, runs-on-its-own. The vote count moved to the detail page.
steps.notice: Stars are gone from cards entirely. Cards with no votes yet show no percent rather than 0%. The glyphs are hidden on phones (the detail page carries them).
steps.risk: A short row on a narrow card can truncate 'what's inside' first; the glyphs stay visible.

steps.headline: Pick a type and the view splits: every skill is its own card, including ones that live inside a plugin.
steps.changed: Before, choosing a type filtered bundles. Now it lists items of that kind — skills from Superpowers appear individually with a 'Part of Superpowers' tag that jumps to the bundle.
steps.notice: The byline reads 'Skill · Anthropic' so each card says what it is. Standalone skills mirrored from GitHub's list sit beside them with the same badges.
steps.risk: The Skills grid is long (22 today, thousands once the catalog is real); the default view stays grouped so this only happens when you ask for a type.

steps.headline: Search finds the skill itself, not just the bundle that contains it.
steps.changed: Typing 'brainstorm' returns the Brainstorming skill (tagged Part of Superpowers) alongside the Superpowers plugin. Before, only the bundle came back and you had to dig.
steps.notice: A chip on its own (a vibe, New, Popular) still shows the grouped view; only typing or picking a type splits things out.
steps.risk: Results can double up — a bundle and three of its skills — when a word matches both. Ranking is by registry order for now.

steps.path: Marketplace → Civic Report → top of the page
steps.headline: The page opens with who made it, whether it was checked, and 'What this can do' — before the description.
steps.changed: Under the title: type and author, the two badges, and where it was mirrored from. Then a plain-words list — connects to the internet (which host), needs a key (which one), saves files where, what it adds.
steps.notice: Install/Uninstall stays where it was; the list sits directly under it so it's read before deciding. Items that do nothing risky say so instead of showing an empty box.
steps.risk: This pushes About and What's inside down one screen on shorter windows.

steps.headline: When the automatic check flags something, the reasons appear inside the same box, in plain words.
steps.changed: Browser Use shows Community · Caution 2, and its list ends with 'The automatic check flagged:' followed by the two findings.
steps.notice: The Install button is unchanged — this informs, it doesn't block. Amber dots, no red, no scary banner.
steps.risk: The findings are written by the scanner; wording quality will vary until the scanner's phrasing rules exist.

steps.path: Marketplace → Civic Report → scroll to the bottom
steps.headline: Reviews became Feedback: one-tap Helpful / Not for me, plus an open comment thread.
steps.changed: The star widget, the 'Write a review' button and the review form are gone. In their place: 'Helpful 93% · 127 votes', two vote buttons, comments with relative dates, and a comment box.
steps.notice: Voting still needs install + sign-in so strangers can't game it. Commenting needs sign-in only, so you can ask a question before installing.
steps.risk: Existing star reviews in the database are not shown anywhere; there are almost none, but the data would be orphaned.

steps.headline: On a phone the seven-way type switch scrolls sideways inside the Filters sheet instead of being cut off.
steps.changed: The Type row in the sheet bleeds to the edges and scrolls; cards keep both badges on one line by showing only the dot for the check status.
steps.notice: The fourth segment peeks in at the right edge as the hint that the row scrolls.
steps.risk: No fade at the edge yet — the peeking segment is the only cue.

steps.headline: What should MCP servers be called in the switch?

options.label: Tools (recommended)
options.summary: Short, and matches how people describe them ('give it a tool that can read my calendar'). The detail page still says 'MCP server' in the fine print.

options.label: Connections
options.summary: Emphasises linking to a service, but overlaps with the Integrations rail ('Connect your stuff') that already exists.

options.label: MCP servers
options.summary: Exact, but jargon — the accessibility rule says a college student shouldn't need to know the acronym.
